Its result sits in its own panel, beside the on-device result and never merged with it — a note states the largest gap between the two, and the downloadable report gains a clearly labelled Gemini section. The honest limits are stated in the tool itself: ticking the box is the only way text ever leaves your device from this tool, the audit uses your key’s Google quota and is slower, and Gemini’s split is still a style estimate, not proof of authorship — Gemini is a language model, it can be inconsistent between runs, and humanized or formal text can fool it like every other detector.

              • In the AI Content Checker (Free Tools → Utilities), the checked text now comes back as a Reviewed text panel with a highlighter over it, sentence by sentence: yellow marks the sentences that read as AI-generated style, grey marks the ones that read as AI-refined / humanized style, and human-typed sentences are left with no highlight. A small key above the text shows the three marks, every sentence is highlighted — not just the strongest ones — and the standout sentences are still listed underneath with the exact reasons each one stood out. The yellow carries dark text of its own, so the highlighting stays readable in Dark, Light, Eye Care and Ocean. The three-way split, the style index and the measurements behind them are unchanged — and the highlighting, like the percentages, marks style resemblance only, never proof of who wrote a sentence.

              • Free Tools → Utilities now opens with an AI Content Checker, built after deep research into ZeroGPT and QuillBot’s detectors and the independent tests of both. Paste any English text (or upload a .txt, or try the built-in Human-written / AI-style / Mixed samples) and you get the split you asked for — % AI-generated style, % AI-refined / humanized style, % human-typed style, always adding to 100% — plus an AI-like style index with its band, the five visible measurements behind it (sentence evenness, predictable words, stock AI phrases, repetition, word variety, with the raw values printed), the text back with its standout sentences shaded and the exact reasons listed, and a copyable / downloadable plain-text report. It is deliberately honest where the big detectors are not: the percentages are labelled style resemblance, not proof of authorship, there is no accuracy claim (ZeroGPT advertises ~98% yet independent tests put it nearer 70–85% and it scored a known human Lewis Carroll passage at 99.6% AI; QuillBot claims 99% yet tests put it nearer 70–78%, and its own humanizer beats its own detector), short text under 40 words gets no score at all instead of false precision, 40–299 words carry a confidence warning, a standing warning explains that humanized or edited AI text scores lower on every detector, and formal, translated or non-native-English writing is called out as scoring higher through no fault of the writer. Like everything on MShop it is free, unlimited, no login, and entirely in your browser — the text is never uploaded, stored or sent anywhere. On phones the result stacks into one column with the three percentages in full-width rows, and every control carries the same small “i” explanation as the other tools.

              • After uploading a photo in the Generator, the next step is now impossible to miss: section 1 · Upload images ends with its own clearly separated action row — a large, highlighted GENERATE button first, then Clear All and Add More. It is an additional row: the Generate metadata for all button in section 2 is still there, and the two Generate buttons are the same button in every way — they run the same generation with the same key, model, platform and settings, they are both disabled when there are no files and while a generation is running, and both show the same Generating… state, so pressing either one can never start a second generation over one already running. Clear All in the new row clears the Generator files and results exactly like the existing Clear all, and Add More opens the same file picker so you can add photos without re-doing the ones already there. The row updates live as files are added, removed, cleared, or arrive from the Shared Tray. Both Generate buttons also share a new solid style: the background comes from your active theme’s own colour profile, so it stays clearly visible with white text in Dark, Light, Eye Care and Ocean alike, with clear hover and focus states, and the disabled state keeps the same theme colour and white text, only muted.

              • Every part of MShop was checked end to end: all scripts syntax-checked, every control and settings reference traced, the CDN libraries’ integrity hashes re-verified against the live files, every view and tool opened and exercised on desktop and phone, and the metadata embeds re-tested byte by byte — including embedding a second time over a file that already carries metadata. Four real bugs were found and fixed. WebP embeds now strip the old EXIF block as well as the old XMP (before, only the XMP was replaced, so an old title or software tag could survive inside a WebP, and the file header could still claim EXIF was present). GIF embeds now remove the metadata blocks already in the file — old comment blocks and Photoshop’s XMP block — before writing the new one, so re-embedding a GIF no longer stacks up comment blocks or leaves the old title inside; the cleanup walks the GIF block by block and, if it meets anything unexpected, leaves the file exactly as it was rather than risk damaging it. JPEG embeds can no longer write a corrupt EXIF segment when the metadata is very large: an EXIF block over the 64 KB segment limit is now refused with a clear warning, the same way the XMP block already was, instead of writing a wrapped segment length. And in the Generator and Trend Hunter, an error page answering for Google (instead of Google’s usual JSON) no longer surfaces as a raw parse error — the HTTP status is kept, so the busy-model retry and model failover keep working. Everything else checked out clean, and no tool, layout or setting changed apart from these fixes. The finished, fixed state of MShop is named v0.2.

              • On phones, the Image Upscaler & Quality Improver, Image Resizer & Crop, Background Remover and Add Watermark now work exactly like the two Compressors: once a photo is loaded, the whole settings area leaves the page and lives in a floating sidebar opened by the gear tab fixed to the right edge — the preview takes the full width, the panel scrolls inside itself over a dim backdrop, and closing it (gear, Hide, Escape or a tap on the dim area) returns you to the exact spot you were reading. Switching tools, sending a file elsewhere or opening the Shared Tray closes it, and opening or closing never resets a setting, a file, a brush stroke, a crop or a watermark position. With no photo loaded there is no gear tab, so the upload area stays fully clear. On desktop nothing changes. Also fixed: the Gemini key panel now opens from every page — the header key used to do nothing outside the Generator and Trend Hunter; the same single floating panel (key box, Save / Remove, session-only option, model picker) now appears over the Compressor, Free Tools, About and every other view, without switching views or losing your scroll position, and saving or removing the key there updates the Generator and Trend Hunter at once, as before. And in the Free Tools index, Watermark Remover and Add Watermark now sit side by side in Image Editing — the two watermark tools together.

              • The PDF Compressor now mirrors the Image Compressor. On desktop the settings panel sits on the left and stays in view while the per-page previews scroll on the right. Under Compression settings there is a Live preview checkbox (on by default), then only Compression mode, Preset and Target Size; everything else — JPEG quality, DPI, grayscale, the remove options and page ranges — folds into a closed More options dropdown that never clears what you set. With Live preview on, settings recompress the checked PDFs live and no Apply button shows. Turn it off and an Apply button appears as the last control at the bottom of the panel — Apply with one file, Apply settings to all with two or more — and nothing reaches the previews until you press it; a plain note says settings have changed meanwhile. The batch buttons (Download Selected / All, Download All as ZIP, Clear All) now appear only with two or more PDFs, while per-PDF Download and remove stay. Every PDF card now has an Apply compression settings checkbox, ticked by default: untick it and that PDF freezes at the settings and compressed version it has at that moment — panel changes and Apply skip it, a “Settings frozen for this PDF” note and its applied-settings summary show on the card, and every download, batch ZIP included, uses the frozen version. Tick it again and it rejoins the panel settings, at once while Live preview is on, or on the next Apply while it is off. On phones, the settings move into a floating sidebar opened by a gear tab fixed to the right edge — it shows only in the PDF Compressor, opens without scrolling the page, and closing it (gear, Hide, Escape or a tap on the dim area) returns you to the exact spot you were reading. Phone previews stack — Original page on top, Compressed below — while size, saving, pages and quality stay side by side in two columns. The compression engine, Safe / Rebuild modes, presets, Target Size ladder, warnings and output checks are unchanged.

              • Every image in the Image Compressor live preview now has an Apply compression settings checkbox, ticked by default. Untick it and that image freezes at the settings and compressed version it has at that moment: changing the panel settings or pressing Apply / Apply settings to all no longer recompresses it, its preview, size, dimensions and format stay put, a plain “Settings frozen for this image” note shows on its card, and every download — its own button, Download All as ZIP, Download All Separately and Save all to tray — uses the frozen version. Tick it again and the image rejoins the panel settings, at once while Live preview is on, or on the next Apply while it is off. If every image is frozen, Apply simply does nothing. On phones, the whole Compression settings panel now lives in a floating sidebar: tap the gear tab fixed to the right edge of the screen (it stays put at every scroll position, and shows only in the Image Compressor) and the settings slide in over a dim backdrop, scrolling inside themselves if tall — the page never scrolls to the top and never loses your place. Close it with the gear tab, the Hide button inside, Escape or a tap on the dim area, and you are back at the exact spot you were reading; switching to the PDF Compressor or sending a file to another tool closes it too. Nothing is reset by opening or closing it, and on desktop nothing changes at all — settings stay in the left column and no gear tab appears. The PDF Compressor was not touched.

              • The Image Compressor settings panel now sits on the left with the preview on the right, and it opens shorter: under Compression settings you see only a new Live preview checkbox (on by default), Output format, Compress by, Quality level and Compression mode (renamed from the old algorithm picker — Standard is still the default). Everything else — width, height, aspect lock and the stock size presets — folds into a closed More options dropdown, and closing it never clears what you set. The old batch recompress button is gone: with Live preview on, settings apply live exactly as before and no Apply button shows at all. Turn Live preview off and an Apply button appears as the last control at the bottom of the settings panel — Apply with one file, Apply settings to all with two or more — and nothing reaches the preview or results until you press it; a plain note says settings have changed meanwhile. The four batch buttons (Download All as ZIP, Download All Separately, Save all to tray, Clear All) now appear only with two or more files — one photo never needs a ZIP — while per-file Download, remove and tray actions stay. Defaults are set once from your screen when the page first loads: desktop starts at WebP and 80% quality; phones start at JPEG and 75%, and resizing or rotating never resets a setting you changed. On phones the preview stacks — Original photo on top, Compressed below — while the size, dimension and format comparison stays side by side in two columns. The compression engine, Target size mode, Compare slider, zoom, magnifier and pan are unchanged, and the PDF Compressor was not touched.

              • Two new strict SEO targets join the Generator: Facebook is now the sixth Target platform tab — the row reads Adobe Stock, Shutterstock, YouTube Thumbnail, Fiverr, LinkedIn, Facebook — and it lives only there, not duplicated in the dropdown; Instagram lives under Other SEO target. Each has its own post pack and alt text panel, rule checklist, SEO score, Submission Readiness and Deep Verify checks, its own CSV (Filename, Post Text / Caption, Alt Text, Hashtags), and a place in the Copy SEO Pack and the Submission Pack. Facebook: primary keyword in the opening line, at most 5 relevant hashtags, and one-line alt text with exactly one keyword phrase, aiming for 125 characters or fewer (a warning over that, not a block). Instagram: caption within 2,200 characters with the primary keyword in the first 125, alt text of at most 100 characters in one sentence, and the 5-hashtag cap enforced even though older guidance allowed more. One plain fact shapes both packs: Facebook and Instagram strip embedded EXIF/IPTC from the publicly served copy on upload, so the embedded title, description and keywords alone will not carry over — the caption and alt text must be entered on the platform itself (on Instagram, via Advanced Settings / More options > Accessibility > Write Alt Text; that alt-text rule is for photo/carousel posts, as Reels have no alt-text box). The embedded download is still the clean file to upload, under a keyword-slug filename. And Trend Hunter now has the same Gemini key panel as the Generator — key box, Save key, session-only option, model picker and the explanations behind its “i”. It is one shared key: save or remove it in the Generator, in Trend Hunter, or in the floating panel, and every place updates at once; once a key is saved, both key areas hide and the header vault key reopens the single floating panel.

              • The Generator settings are shorter to scan. The model picker is now simply Select model (the free-tier note lives behind its “i”), and the no-key explanation moved behind the key panel’s “i” too. Once your Gemini key is saved, the key panel hides itself — tap the vault key in the header and it reappears as a floating panel over the page, with the key box, Save key, the session-only option and the model picker; close it with its ×, a tap outside, Escape or the header key again, and your saved key is untouched. The Target platform row keeps five everyday targets — Adobe Stock, Shutterstock, YouTube Thumbnail, Fiverr, LinkedIn — and every other target now lives under Other SEO target, with the same rules, tips and scores; Add your own SEO target is a fold-away section. Title length and Keywords can be typed as well as slid (on phones only the typed box shows). Everything after Keywords — stock size, language, category, custom prompt, rights & credits — folds into More settings/options. The Submission Pack ZIP button moved beside Generate metadata for all and unlocks once a result exists, and section 3’s export buttons now appear only when there are results to export: Copy / Download CSV and Embed and download with the first result, plus Embed and Download ZIP when two or more files are ready.

              • Two phone-only fixes. In the Generator, the Progress & results bar no longer sticks to the top of the screen while you scroll when there is nothing to show: with no results and nothing generating, it is hidden completely. It appears the moment a generation starts — with the live percentage, the current step, elapsed and estimated time, and how many files are finished and ready — stays while your results are there (tap View results to jump to them), and hides again when the results are cleared and the Generator is idle. And the Shared tray on phones is now a floating panel: tap the header cart from anywhere on the page — even the very bottom — and the full tray opens over the page without scrolling you back to the top; if the tray is tall it scrolls inside itself. Close it with Hide, the cart, Escape or a tap on the dimmed area, and you land back at the exact spot you were reading. The red file-count badge, every tray action, and the desktop slide-in tray are all unchanged.

              • On phones, the header’s right side is now cart, key, theme, menu: a new cart icon — the same cart as the desktop tray tab — sits before the key icon. The tray no longer sits at the top of every page on phones: tap the cart and the Shared tray appears at the top, exactly as it looked there before, and a new Hide button inside the tray hides it again (tapping the cart again works too). Both cart icons — the phone header cart and the desktop side tab — carry the same red circular badge with a white number: the live count of files in the tray, hidden while the tray is empty and updated the moment a file is added, removed or cleared. And the tray’s file area is bigger: it now takes PDFs as well as photos. Add PDFs with the tray’s Add files button, or open a PDF in any PDF tool and it joins the tray automatically; a PDF made with Image → PDF joins too. PDFs show as red PDF tiles, keep their versions, save in your browser and download through the Download Centre and ZIP exactly like photos — and selected PDFs can be sent straight to the PDF Compressor or PDF → Image, while photo tools simply skip them (and PDF tools skip photos) with a plain note. The count at the top of the tray now reads as files — for example “5 files · 3 photos · 2 PDFs”. Desktop is otherwise unchanged: its tray stays the right-side slide-in bar.

              • On desktop, the Shared tray no longer sits as a wide panel between the header and the tools, eating the top of every page — the tools now start directly under the header. The tray moved to a slide-in bar on the right side: click the cart tab fixed to the right edge of the screen — it stays in the same place however far you scroll — and the tray slides in with everything it had before (photos, versions, Download Centre, workflows). The tab shows a badge with the photo count, rides to the tray’s edge while it is open, and closes it again; you can also close it with the Close button, the dimmed area beside it, or Escape. Sending photos to a tool closes the tray for you, so you land straight on the tool. Inside, photos wrap in two columns instead of one long sideways strip. Phones are unchanged for now — the tray stays at the top there until its own mobile pass.

              • On phones, the lighter right half of the Compressor and Free Tools rows no longer shows the word Menu — it shows only the triangle arrow, now a little bigger so it is easy to see and tap. Nothing else changed: the right half still only opens the dropdown, the left half still goes straight to the section, and the desktop caret is slightly larger too.

              • On phones, tapping Compressor or Free Tools in the opened menu used to go straight to that section, so the dropdown was hard to reach — the arrow was tiny. Those two rows are now split 50 / 50: tap the left half to go to the section itself, or tap the right half — shown in a slightly lighter colour and labelled Menu — to open its dropdown, which now opens right under the row. The left half never opens the dropdown and the right half never navigates, so the two can no longer be mixed up. Generator and Trend Hunter have no dropdown, so they keep their normal full-width rows, and the desktop header is unchanged.

              • On phones, the header dropdowns (Compressor and Free Tools) no longer react to hover at all: they open only when you tap the small arrow, and stay open until you tap an item, tap outside, or press Escape — a menu can never pop open or vanish by itself while you move around the bar, and a tapped item no longer stays highlighted. Desktop keeps its hover menus exactly as before. The Gemini key icon is new too: a vault key, its round handle drawn as a little vault dial, in the same place on desktop and phone — still yellow on phones while no key is saved and green once yours is.

              • About Us and What’s New are gone from the top menu — they live in the footer now, one tap away on every page, and nothing else about them changed. On phones the header is no longer crowded: it shows only the logo on the left and three icons on the right — the Gemini key icon (yellow while no key is saved, green once yours is), the theme icon (tap it and pick by icon alone: moon for Dark, sun for Light, glasses for Eye Care, waves for Ocean), and the menu icon, which opens the same main menu as on desktop. The desktop header keeps its full layout, with the four main choices: Generator, Compressor, Trend Hunter and Free Tools.

              • In Image ⇄ PDF → PDF → Image, pressing Render Pages (unchanged) now shows each page in a large live preview the moment it finishes rendering, while the rest keep rendering. Zoom in on the preview with + / − from Fit through 50% to 300% — or focus it and use the keyboard — then drag to look around when zoomed; tap any small photo (or its new View button) to preview that page. Zoom changes only the preview, never the downloaded photo. The Download All as ZIP button no longer sits beside Render: it stays hidden while pages render and appears below the last rendered photo once every page is done, with a note confirming all pages are ready. Each photo keeps its own Download button, exactly as before.

              • The Free Tools dropdown in the top bar now ends with a View more tools → link, under the four everyday tools. It opens the full Free Tools page — every tool, grouped by category — so the whole list is one click away from the menu itself, not only from the Free Tools button. Nothing else in the menu changed.

              • The Free Tools dropdown in the top bar now shows only the four everyday tools: Image Upscaler, Resize / Crop, BG Remover and Image ⇄ PDF. Nothing was removed — every other tool is still on the Free Tools page itself; open Free Tools (not the small arrow) for the full list. The old Image to PDF is renamed Image ⇄ PDF — the ⇄ is a two-headed arrow, because the section now works in both directions, in one card, switched exactly like the Image Compressor and PDF Compressor: Image → PDF combines your images into one PDF, and PDF → Image turns a PDF’s pages into JPG or PNG images at 72–300 DPI, one by one or all as a ZIP. Switching direction never clears your files or results in either converter, and the PDF Compressor’s More PDF tools → PDF to Image button now opens this same card on the PDF → Image side. All of it stays free, unlimited, and entirely in your browser.

              • The top menu is now just Generator, Compressor, Trend Hunter, Free Tools and About Us — easier to read at a glance, and much simpler on phones. Background Remover and Watermark Remover moved into Free Tools → Image Tools, at the top of that list and in the Image Editing section of the Free Tools page. What’s New now lives in the new About Us dropdown — hover or tap the small arrow beside About Us, exactly like the Compressor menu. Nothing was removed: every tool works exactly as before, only the menu is cleaner and more modern.

              • Free Tools → Image Editing now ends with a Photopea card for the times you need full Photoshop-style editing — layers, PSD files and advanced retouching. Photopea is a free online photo editor on its own site; it is not part of MShop. The clearly labelled Open Photopea button opens photopea.com in a new tab, and anything you edit there is handled by Photopea, not by MShop.

              • Resizer & Crop (and the new Image Editor below) now shrink photos with a stepped resize engine: instead of one crude jump from full size straight to the target — the jump that makes edges look blocky and pixelated — the photo is halved repeatedly with high-quality smoothing until it is within one step of the target, then drawn once to the exact size, always from the full-resolution original in your browser, transparency kept. The tool shows the real encoded output size (never an estimate) with the % saved, a percentage slider and 50% / 25% presets beside the existing size presets, an optional mild Sharpen after resize, and Fit / 100% / 200% preview zoom so you can judge sharpness on the same area before downloading. Resize never enlarges: a request bigger than the original is clamped to the original size with a plain note, because enlarging cannot add detail — the Upscaler remains the place for that. New Crop only (no resize) mode copies the rectangle you drag pixel-for-pixel at native resolution — no resampling at all — and switches the export to PNG, showing the kept dimensions and “kept pixels unchanged”; if you then resize the kept area, the order is stated on the panel: crop first at native resolution, then the stepped resize. One honest note: stepped resizing preserves the sharpness that is in your photo — it does not invent new detail, and a JPG or WebP download still re-encodes, which is why Crop only defaults to lossless PNG and why chained edits are best kept on the tray’s Original / Worked versions instead of re-uploading a downloaded JPG.

              • Free Tools → Image Editing now has an Image Editor, built after studying what people actually use in classic online editors, and refined the MShop way: entirely in your browser, free and unlimited, no login, nothing uploaded, every explanation behind an “i” icon. Load a photo and the tools appear: Basics — Resize (the stepped engine above), Crop (native, pixel-for-pixel, with drag box, numbers, aspect presets and a thirds grid), Rotate / Flip (quarter turns swap the dimensions exactly; custom angles grow the canvas), Colour Adjust (brightness, contrast, saturation, sharpen, plus Normalise / Auto-levels, Sepia, Grayscale, B&W, Equalise and Invert), Text (MShop’s fonts plus system fonts, stroke, arc and shadow, drag to place) and Convert (PNG / JPG / WebP with quality — and a plain note that an edited animated GIF becomes a still image, because canvas editing keeps only the first frame). Advanced — Border (outline grows the canvas, stated on the panel; raised / lowered bevels), Round Corners, Vignette / Passe-Partout, click-colour Transparency with Fuzz (labelled honestly as colour matching, not a background remover — the Background Remover stays the tool for that), Overlay Image, Expand Canvas, Cut Shapes, Speech Bubble, Photo Frame (simple drawn frames, no external pictures) and Image in Text. Every tool previews live before you press Apply, Undo / Redo step through applied edits, the tray Original is never overwritten, and Resize / Crop / Rotate / Colour / Convert can be applied to a whole batch with per-file and ZIP downloads.

              • Thank you for the report — it was reproduced and traced. The presets were being applied, but in the default Safe / Keep text mode the file is only re-saved: its page images are never re-encoded, and presets set image quality and DPI, so on a scanned or image-heavy PDF every preset produced a file within a few bytes of the original — the preview and the download looked like the original because, page for page, they were. Nothing on the card explained that. Now, whenever a Safe-mode result saves under 1% on an image PDF, the card says exactly why, and offers a one-tap Switch this file to Rebuild pages button; on text PDFs it explains that the content is already compact and Rebuild would usually make it larger. Presets in Rebuild pages mode worked and still work — that is where quality and DPI bite (in testing, a 5.1 MB scanned PDF went to about 0.5 MB on Maximum). As before, a failed compression shows the exact error on the card and disables that file's download — the original is never silently handed back labelled as compressed.

              • Both compressors now have a Target size mode beside the quality controls. For PDFs: type a maximum size (or tap 100 KB, 200 KB, 300 KB, 500 KB, 1 MB, 2 MB — the classic case: a 3 MB PDF that must fit a 200 KB upload limit) and MShop searches honestly: a Safe re-save first, then Rebuild pages from best quality downwards (300 DPI Q85 through 72 DPI Q25, with grayscale as an optional last step), stopping at the first real file at or under your target and showing the attempts, the winning settings and the achieved size. If the target cannot be reached — text-heavy PDFs have a floor, because there is little image data to shrink — you get the closest result with a clear warning, never a padded or truncated file pretending to be the target. Targets can be set per file, and batch / ZIP downloads work as before. The Image Compressor gets the same idea: a target in KB (chips for 20 / 50 / 100 / 200 KB), searching quality first and then smaller dimensions — never larger — with the same honest closest-result warning. Like everything here: free, unlimited, and entirely in your browser.

              • Free Tools → Media & Downloads (and the new More PDF tools bar inside the PDF Compressor) now has a full PDF toolkit, all running in your browser with pdf-lib and pdf.js — no upload, no server, free and unlimited: Merge PDF (drag to reorder, total page count), Split / Extract Pages (ranges like 1-3,5, as one PDF or separate one-page PDFs in a ZIP), Rotate PDF (90 / 180 / 270°, all pages or a range, text stays selectable), Organize / Remove Pages (page thumbnails, drag to reorder, delete pages), Extract Images (every embedded image at stored resolution — JPEGs stored as JPEG come out byte-for-byte; anything converted is labelled converted), PDF to Image (every page or a range to JPG / PNG at 72–300 DPI), Add Page Numbers (six positions, starting number, font size, “Page X of Y”, live preview), and Crop PDF (drag a crop box on the preview or type margins — cropping hides the area outside the box; the hidden content still exists in the file, and the tool says so). Every output is re-opened and page-count checked before its download enables, and password-protected or corrupted PDFs get a plain error, here as everywhere on MShop.

              • Free Tools → Media & Downloads now has an Advanced PDF Compressor, built like CompressPro but for PDFs — and entirely in your browser: no PDF is ever uploaded anywhere. Drop one PDF or a batch and each file is analysed first — page count, PDF version, selectable text, embedded images, fonts, annotations / comments, embedded files, document metadata and bookmarks — so you can see why a file will or will not shrink before it starts. Compression is live: change any setting and every file recompresses with per-page progress and a Cancel button, showing the real compressed byte size (never an estimate) beside the original, the % saved (or % larger, stated honestly), and a size bar; every output is re-opened and its page count verified before its Download button enables. Two modes: Safe / Keep text (rebuilt with pdf-lib — object streams, plus optional removal of metadata, annotations, attachments and bookmarks; text and vectors stay intact, and savings are usually small on image-heavy files) and Rebuild pages (each page rendered with pdf.js and re-encoded as JPEG at your DPI and quality — big savings on scans, but text becomes part of the page image, with a clear warning on the card when the source had selectable text). A per-page quality preview compares any page Original vs Compressed side by side or with a drag slider, at Fit / 100% / 200%, with a quality label taken from your actual settings. Plus presets (Light, Balanced, Strong, Maximum), an Advanced section (JPEG quality, max DPI 72–300, grayscale, content removals, custom page ranges like 1-3,5 with out-of-range pages rejected with a message), per-file custom settings, batch Download Selected / Download All / Download as ZIP, and plain per-file errors for password-protected, corrupted or empty PDFs. Free and unlimited, no login.

              • When Google answers that a model is “currently experiencing high demand” (503) or rate-limits your key (429), generation no longer fails the file on the spot. MShop now retries with a spaced-out backoff — honouring any Retry-After delay Google sends — and then automatically tries the next Gemini Flash model in the picker, in order, while the live status tells you which model is busy and which model is being tried. Your uploaded file and all its settings are kept exactly as they are, and your selected model is never changed permanently — failover is per generation only. If every model stays busy, the file is marked failed with a Retry button on its card and a Retry failed button for the whole batch. So the failure never looks like a broken website, a plain-words banner and the failed file’s card both explain that the model is busy on Google’s side, that MShop is working fine and your photo and settings are still here, name the busy model and the alternatives to try, and offer Retry plus a Try another model button that takes you straight to the model picker; the banner stays until a generation succeeds or you dismiss it, and Trend Hunter shows the same guidance. One honest note: these limits are Google’s model demand and free-tier rate limits on your own key — MShop adds no limits of its own — and the spikes are usually temporary, so retrying a few minutes later normally works. Trend Hunter and the Background Remover’s Gemini subject guide get the same automatic retry and failover.

              • Right-click is still blocked everywhere it was before, but now the first three blocked right-clicks in a visit show a small popup beside your cursor — “Right-click is blocked for privacy.” — which fades away on its own after a few seconds, or on your next click, a scroll, or Escape. From the fourth right-click onwards the menu is blocked silently: no popup, no menu, no matter how many times you try. The count is kept only for the current browser session (session storage) and resets when the tab session ends; right-click inside a text field still opens its edit menu, so pasting your Gemini key keeps working. As always, this is a deterrent against casual copying, not total security — no web page can make its code truly uncopyable. The About Us page now has a clear Privacy section listing every privacy feature MShop actually offers: free with no account or login; all tools running in your browser with no photo uploaded to an MShop server; Shared Tray photos stored only in your own browser (IndexedDB) with Pause browser saving / Clear saved photos controls and a kept-only-until-reload fallback; your Gemini key entered in the app, stored only in your browser (with a session-only option), never asked for in chat, never sent to MShop, and sent only to Google for generation; browser-only generation history with delete controls; embedded downloads that strip the old metadata and write only the new metadata you approve; and right-click blocking described honestly as a deterrent only. A copyright note for the MShop name, logo, design and site content now appears in About Us and in the footer.

              • Result cards are now compact above the download button: only the Title, Description and Keywords fields, plus the SEO Direct Injector with a short format · target label. Everything else moved below the Embed & Download button into collapsed sections that show just their heading — tap or click the heading (or its chevron) to reveal the full content, tap again to fold it away. In order: Image quality — measured on this device, Gemini quality estimate, SEO checklist (heading carries the target and score, e.g. LinkedIn 93/100), Submission Readiness, Deep AI Content Verify (heading carries its score and Pass / Needs fix / Fail badge), the platform pack, the Recreation prompt, Copy actions, and Download details (format, size, SEO target, writes). An Expand all / Collapse all control sits under the download button, scores in the headings keep updating as you edit, and nothing was removed — every checklist, pack, prompt and button works exactly as before once its section is open. One placement change: the LinkedIn alt text now lives inside the LinkedIn post pack & alt text section together with the post text and hashtags (still LinkedIn-only, still with its live character count, Copy and Use-title buttons, and still included in the LinkedIn copy pack and CSV).

              • Two new SEO targets in a new Freelance & Social group, built to each platform’s strict rules rather than as name-only labels. Fiverr: Gemini returns a full gig pack — a gig title starting exactly “I will” within 80 characters with the primary keyword and a differentiator in the first 60–65 and no & / + characters, a 120–1200 character gig description (hook, what’s included, process, call to action; no URLs, contact details or unverifiable claims), exactly 5 search tags of at most 20 characters that complement the title, and a keyword-slug gallery filename (downloads use it automatically) — with gallery guidance (1280×769 recommended, 712×430 min, 4000×2416 max, under 5MB, 40px safe zone), a warning that the gig URL is fixed from the first published title, a Fiverr rule checklist on every result, a Fiverr CSV, and the pack included in Copy SEO Pack and the Submission Pack. LinkedIn: a post pack (hook in the first line, within 3000 characters, short paragraphs, 3–5 hashtags, image guidance 1200×627 / 1200×1200 / 1080×1350) plus a dedicated LinkedIn alt text box — which has since moved into the LinkedIn post pack & alt text section below the download button — editable, with a live character count (max 1000, aim 100–200), a Copy button, and an “i” note explaining it must be pasted into LinkedIn’s own Alt text field because LinkedIn strips embedded EXIF. The alt panel appears only while LinkedIn is the selected target; switching away hides it without deleting the text. Deep AI Content Verify now runs on every generated result, on every target, in a panel directly below that file’s download button: platform-rule compliance, trademark / brand risk (Gemini’s flag plus a local brand scan), spelling & grammar, AI artefacts & quality (Gemini audit plus the on-device pixel measurement), keyword stuffing / near-duplicates / misleading claims, metadata completeness, an embedded-file re-read (the Re-verify button embeds in memory and reads the file back, checking the new fields are present and old / AI-origin / software markers are stripped from the metadata), and AI-disclosure readiness with a ready-to-paste line. It shows a 0–100 score with a Pass / Needs fix / Fail badge, one-line fixes, and re-checks live as you edit. One honest note it prints on every result: clean metadata does not guarantee pixel-based detectors or platform review will miss AI origin, and stock platforms require AI disclosure. Everything stays free, unlimited, no login.

              • MShop's code was audited and hardened end to end, with zero cost to speed. Your Gemini key is safer: it is now sent to Google in a request header instead of the web address (so it can no longer leak through address bars, browser history or logs), it is no longer written back into the key box after saving, and a new Session only option in the key panel keeps it only until you close the tab — nothing is written to the device's saved storage, the right choice on a shared computer. The page itself is locked down: the three helper libraries (ZIP, PDF, QR) now load with cryptographic integrity checks, so a tampered copy would be refused by your browser; a Content Security Policy limits the page to loading code, fonts and images only from MShop itself, cdnjs, Google Fonts, Google's Gemini API and YouTube thumbnails — and blocks plug-ins and form posts to anywhere else; and a no-referrer policy stops your browsing here leaking to sites you click out to. Your downloads are safer too: exported SVGs now have all active content stripped (scripts, event handlers, embedded frames and external references), so a file you embed here can never run code when opened, and CSV exports neutralise spreadsheet formula tricks in titles and keywords. Copy protection: right-click and the usual inspect / view-source shortcuts are now blocked, like on other professional tool sites. One honest note, because we would rather tell you than oversell it: this is a deterrent against casual copying — no website on earth can make its code truly uncopyable, since the browser must receive the code to run it. The real security is the part above: this page holds no secrets at all, your files and photos never leave your browser except the one analysis copy you choose to send to Gemini, and your key is yours alone. Also new: colour themes. The picker in the top bar offers four themes built for MShop — Dark (the current look, still the default), Light, Eye Care (warm, low-glare, softer contrast for long sessions) and Ocean (a deep dark-blue variant). Switching is instant: every colour on the page comes from one set of variables, so there is nothing extra to load and nothing slows down. Your choice is saved in your browser and applied before the page paints, the MShop logo swaps to the version that stays readable on light and dark backgrounds, status colours, image stages and the transparency checkerboard all stay readable in every theme, and the CompressPro panel warms up to match in Eye Care.

              • Free Tools → Image Editing now has a dedicated Image Upscaler & Quality Improver: upscale 2×, 3×, 4× or a custom scale with high-quality multi-pass scaling, plus sharpen / detail, denoise / smoothing and clarity / contrast controls, a draggable Original / Enhanced compare slider with 100% and 200% zoom for checking detail, downloads at exactly the size shown (JPG, PNG or WebP), batch + ZIP, and tray sends to the Compressor and Generator. It is honest about its limit, in its own “i” note: it sharpens and restores perceived detail from the pixels in your photo — it cannot invent true detail that was never captured the way a large AI super-resolution model attempts to. The Resizer & Crop tool gains an Improve quality — Upscaler button beside its other send buttons, carrying the current photo (Original or Worked, as chosen in the tray) straight into the new tool. And the Background Remover now shows a short note under the result — only after a cut-out has been generated — pointing to bgeraser.com and remove.bg as alternative removers if a result disappoints, with an Improve quality in MShop button that sends the cut-out straight to the new upscaler, in case an external tool saved your photo at reduced quality. Everything stays free, unlimited, no login, and entirely in your browser.

              • The Background Remover no longer greets you with every option at once. It opens on just the photo drop area; once a photo is loaded you get the preview plus one easy Removal effect slider that re-runs the removal live as you drag it, a Download and a Re-run button. Everything else is under Advanced options, grouped by category: Detection (sensitivity, subject mode, saturated-colour and interior safeguards, the optional Gemini subject guide), Edge & Hair, Brushes & Fixes, Selection (Custom Area Select), and Output & Size (background, presets, size, format & quality, batch and chain downloads). Nothing was removed — it is all still there, folded away until you need it. Also fixed: the header Background Remover button now opens only the Background Remover (it used to land on the whole Free Tools list), and every tool now opens in a focused view — opening a tool from the header, the Free Tools index, the new Free Tools header dropdown (Image Tools, Download Tools, Utilities), or a Shared Tray send shows only that tool, so scrolling can never drift into another tool. An All tools button returns to the index, and the Shared Tray still carries your photo — Original or Worked — straight into the next tool. Header, tray and footer stay visible throughout.

              • Generation no longer sits at 88% for 40+ seconds. That stall was never the SEO check: the deep SEO audit is local and takes under a second. The wait was the Gemini reply, slowed mainly by sending the untouched full-resolution photo. MShop now sends Gemini a fast analysis copy (long edge capped at 1280px — the same detail Gemini's vision actually uses for metadata) while your original file stays untouched for embedding and download, measures the photo's pixel quality in parallel instead of afterwards, and asks Gemini for tighter recreation-prompt wording so the reply is shorter. The progress bar now creeps while it waits on Gemini instead of parking on one number, says so honestly, and only enters the “Deep SEO audit & quality” step when the reply actually lands. The audit itself is deeper than before: keyword coverage across title + description, primary-keyword position in the title, top keywords echoed in the description, long-tail keyword mix, near-duplicate keyword forms, keyword-stuffing detection, natural-title formatting, and whether the download filename will be SEO-ready — on top of every check it already ran.

              • Section 3 — Results & export — and the analysis progress panel no longer stay behind at the top while you scroll through the Generator settings and file list. On desktop the whole progress + results column (CSV platform, Copy CSV, Download CSV, Embed & Download ZIP, Submission Pack ZIP and the results list) stays pinned in view below the header while the settings scroll, and its own list scrolls inside the pinned column when it grows tall. On phones a compact sticky bar shows the live progress %, current step, elapsed / estimated time left, finished count and how many results are ready, with a View results jump to section 3. Progress, results and all downloads update live exactly as before.

              • Every result now shows two separate quality figures: a local Image quality measurement computed from the photo's own pixels on your device (dimensions / megapixels, sharpness, exposure and brightness distribution, clipped shadows and highlights, noise, texture) and Gemini's score, now clamped to 0–100 and clearly labelled an AI estimate. Embedding can now also write your own optional creator / author, copyright / rights, credit line and category (EXIF Artist / Copyright, XMP creator / rights / credit / category, IPTC on JPEG, XMP + eXIf on PNG), the source ICC colour profile is preserved on JPEG and PNG, an on-screen warning appears if XMP ever has to be dropped for size, and WebP and GIF downloads now keep their own format instead of being silently converted to JPEG. The recreation prompt is now a full panel: an editable prompt built from subject, composition, lighting, style, colours, background, camera and mood, Exact recreate / Similar / Different angle-style variations, a negative prompt, an aspect and size suggestion from the photo's dimensions, and copy buttons formatted for Midjourney, DALL·E, Stable Diffusion and Firefly / Leonardo, plus Copy all and Download prompts — for use in external AI image generators; MShop does not generate the image itself.

              • Photos in the shared tray are saved in your own browser only (IndexedDB on your device) — never on a server. Reload the page, close the tab, or open a new tab in the same browser and your photos, every version, your Original / Worked choice and your selection are restored. The tray shows “Photos saved in this browser” when saving is on, and “Photos kept only until reload” when it is paused or unavailable, with Pause / Resume and Clear saved photos controls in the tray. If browser storage is full or unavailable, uploads and all tools keep working and photos are simply kept until reload.

              • The Background Remover is back to the Classic edge-detection engine as the only engine: the BiRefNet AI model and its ~109 MB download are gone, so removal is instant again, with every brush, safeguard, Custom Area Select, preset, batch mode and download unchanged. The optional Gemini subject guide stays — off by default, using only the Gemini key already saved in your browser — and now guides Classic in hard cases while Classic still makes the final cut-out; any Gemini failure falls back to Classic alone with the exact error shown. Also new: in every image tool the preview now stays in view while you scroll the options, so you no longer change settings blindly — and if you reload the page, MShop reopens on the tool you were using, with your tray photos restored from your browser as before.

              • The Background Remover now defaults to a real AI matting model — BiRefNet-lite (MIT licence) — running entirely in your browser with Transformers.js, using WebGPU where available and WebAssembly as the fallback. Like remove.bg, it understands the subject (person, clothes, animals, products) instead of matching colours, and returns a soft alpha matte, so hair and fur keep their fine strands; edge colours are decontaminated so cut-outs do not carry a background-colour halo. The model downloads once (about 115 MB with WebGPU, 224 MB on the WASM path), stays cached in your browser, and no photo is ever uploaded. The previous edge-detection remover remains as the Classic engine — instant, with no download — and every brush, Custom Area Select, preset, batch mode and download works on the AI matte exactly as before.

              • Upload once into the shared tray and send the same photo to every tool — Original or Worked version, your choice — with a version history per photo, one-click workflow recipes and a Download Centre. The Compressor is now compression-only: no upscaling (dimensions scale down only) and no watermark options; watermarking lives in its own new Add Watermark tool. Resizer & Crop adds upscale/downscale, presets, Photoshop-style crop inside a fixed frame, free drag-rectangle crop, Fit fills and rotate/flip. Add Watermark adds seven ready-made designs plus a Custom design with an Advanced CSS section, five professional text colours, drag positioning, batch use and browser-only presets.

              • CompressPro’s feature blurbs and three-step guide now sit behind its “i” icon, the Generator’s SEO rules for the selected target sit behind an “i” beside the label, and the duplicate About link at the top of the Generator is gone — so every working view opens straight onto the controls.

              • Opening the site now goes straight to the work — the long introductions at the top are gone. Every explanation sits behind an “i” icon beside its control, the full story moved to About Us, and this What’s New page records each update.

              • Renamed from StockMeta to MShop, with the MShop logo adapted for the dark site (blue gradient kept, dark lettering made light), the logo alone in the top header, and the desktop header fit fixed so every menu item is fully visible.

              • Each result now shows the original on the left and the compressed image live on the right, with original size, compressed size, dimensions, format and percentage saved underneath, plus a compare slider. In the Generator, the SEO file-name download option is now on by default and can be changed at any time.

              • The background is now sampled from patches along the whole edge and clustered, so a subject touching one corner can no longer be treated as background. Saturated colours and enclosed interior foreground are protected by default, and Fix subject repairs any damaged subject area.

              • Background removal can be limited to a rectangle, lasso or brush-painted area, with invert and feather. Force Remove and Protect Foreground brushes persist across re-runs, alongside Magic Wand, Lasso, Fill Holes, Remove Isolated Islands, Keep Largest Subject, mask views and per-stroke undo / redo.

              • Patch-based inpainting that copies real texture and edges from the best-matching surrounding patches — not blur — with colour and grain matching, Clone Stamp and Healing Brush, a donor-area control, and an automatic quality check.

              • Live analysis progress with step-by-step status, 21 SEO targets with a live SEO score and checklist plus a Direct Injector, a one-click Submission Pack (embedded images, all platform CSVs, copy pack and readiness report), a Metadata Verifier that re-reads embedded files, a Submission Readiness Checker and browser-only local History.

              • The Generator and Trend Hunter default to Gemini 3.8 Flash on the Google AI Studio free tier, with Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 and 3.1 Flash-Lite and 3 Flash Preview also available. Google’s free-tier rate limits still apply per project and key.
